title: The Impunity Machine
dek: A visual data investigation into Bangladesh's rape justice crisis and the institutional machinery that turns reported violence into near-zero punishment.
summary: A forensic visual investigation tracing Bangladesh's rape justice crisis across reporting attrition, conviction rates, court backlog, forensic capacity, and legal data voids.
key_findings: Only 310 convictions were recorded from 66,711 women who came through One-Stop Crisis Centres over 23 years, a 0.46% conviction rate.
Bangladesh pairs maximum legal severity with near-zero certainty of punishment: death penalty expansion did not solve reporting attrition, backlog, evidence loss, or witness risk.
Critical justice infrastructure remains thin: 14 OCCs, two national DNA machines, major unprocessed sample backlogs, and no complete national registry for key rape-case outcomes.
